reason: Test the small, source-expressible changes first. Keeping scratch reserved changes stack handling but leaves packing and arithmetic intact; interleaving the ZA tile operations keeps each tile’s K order; and using a W counter is a narrow loop-control test. None has measured evidence of a gain, and the counter change may compile to equivalent code. The fused transpose path avoids about 16 MiB of packed-A reads, but repeats A loading and transpose work across 16 column panels: about 1 MiB of A traffic becomes about 16 MiB, with higher mapping and correctness risk. The B-panel path adds repeated packing and coordinated traversal edits. The last two proposals are duplicates in substance and both need an unavailable N=64 generated helper, so they are not currently implementable. Historical noisy scores do not establish a winner or explain any outcome.
